paper_title: First indirect detection constraints on axions in the Solar basin
notes: Paper sets first indirect-detection limits on solar-basin axions decaying to X-rays, using NuSTAR quiescent solar limb observations. Main result relevant here is Fig. 2: 90% CL limits on g_agamma (with g_aee=0) for m = 3-40 keV, world-leading for 5-30 keV, improving on horizontal branch star cooling (~6.6e-11 GeV^-1) by over an order of magnitude. No numerical table is provided in the text; the data_points above are approximate values inferred from the figure axis ranges (1e-12 to 1e-9 GeV^-1) and the stated >10x improvement over HB cooling, with the characteristic weakening at low masses (4 keV energy cutoff) and high masses (production suppression near 2*m_e*sigma ~ 50 keV). The paper also constrains g_aee and the universal-coupling f slice (Fig. 1), but the photon coupling (Fig. 2) is the cleanest single-coupling result. Not a dark-matter haloscope; no local DM density assumed (signal is from Sun-produced bound axions).
